patterns.pattern: Access to administrator and moderation dashboards or tools is restricted to users with designated elevated roles.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only admins can view or use administrative dashboards and tools.

patterns.pattern: User roles and permissions are configurable by administrators, determining feature and content access.
patterns.example_phrasing: Admins can set user roles and permissions for different actions or content.

patterns.pattern: Private or restricted channels and content must be explicitly subscribed to or permitted for user access; guests need explicit subscription.
patterns.example_phrasing: Guest users must subscribe to private channels to access them.

patterns.pattern: Account and username deletion or changes are irreversible and usernames remain reserved.
patterns.example_phrasing: Deleted accounts cannot be restored and their usernames stay unusable.

patterns.pattern: User registration can require valid email and/or manual approval based on administrator settings.
patterns.example_phrasing: Admins may require email verification or approval for new registrations.

patterns.pattern: Content visibility settings (e.g., NSFW, public/members-only) are user-configurable or set by editors/admins.
patterns.example_phrasing: Users can configure visibility of sensitive content in their feed.

patterns.pattern: Administrative users can configure or restrict certain actions (e.g., channel creation, invites, plugin settings, moderation actions).
patterns.example_phrasing: Admins can decide who may create channels or invite others.

patterns.pattern: Moderators or admins have authority to ban, mute or deactivate abusive, spam, or troll users.
patterns.example_phrasing: Moderators can ban users who violate community rules.

patterns.pattern: Federation features: users can follow communities or content across federated instances.
patterns.example_phrasing: Users can follow and subscribe to posts from other federated communities.

patterns.pattern: Action limits and anti-abuse mechanisms (e.g., limiting registrations per day, filtering duplicate inputs) prevent spam and abuse.
patterns.example_phrasing: Users can only register once per day to prevent abuse.

patterns.pattern: Sensitive administrative panels (e.g., ACP) must be protected from unauthorized access.
patterns.example_phrasing: The admin control panel should only be visible to authorized admins.

patterns.pattern: State changes or deletions in system components (e.g., plugin disabling, extension removal, account moves) may be irreversible, often requiring caution or explicit confirmation.
patterns.example_phrasing: Removing extensions or disabling plugins is irreversible and requires explicit confirmation.

patterns.pattern: Scheduling and job posting features can expire or require reactivation after a set period (e.g., job ads expire after 30 days).
patterns.example_phrasing: Job postings expire after 30 days unless extended.

patterns.pattern: Content moderation tools filter spam, inappropriate content (e.g., nudity, copyright infringement), and automate premoderation.
patterns.example_phrasing: Admins can automatically filter offensive or abusive content.

patterns.pattern: Profile, session, and account transitions transfer limited information; some data types are excluded from moves.
patterns.example_phrasing: When an account is moved, only followers transfer; posts and bookmarks do not.

patterns.pattern: Key configuration dependencies: certain features (e.g., registration, notification) only work if required configurations (e.g., email) are valid.
patterns.example_phrasing: User registration requires valid email configuration.

patterns.pattern: Content recommendation and notifications are personalized based on user profiles and activity.
patterns.example_phrasing: Recommended content is tailored to each user’s profile and news events.

patterns.pattern: All user-generated changes (e.g., content, documentation edits) are encouraged via an open contribution model (pull requests).
patterns.example_phrasing: All edits to documentation are welcome and should be submitted via pull request.
